key_insight: A guideline-augmented multi-agent workflow can make biomedical named entity recognition more accurate by turning ambiguous annotations into schema-constrained, verifiable entity outputs.
clinical_relevance: This could improve the reliability of biomedical text mining pipelines used to structure literature, support downstream curation, and reduce annotation errors in clinical NLP workflows.
method: Induce dataset-specific annotation rules from labeled examples and verify them to build a guideline memory.
Use a planning agent to generate ranked span-type hypotheses with rationales.
Convert hypotheses into schema-constrained entities, then verify and refine them with dual-loop checking for grounding, type validity, and format compliance.
evidence_signal: The approach was evaluated on five widely used BioNER datasets across multiple LLM backbones and consistently outperformed strong LLM-based baselines.
watch_item: The framework depends on high-quality labeled data and verified guidelines, so performance may be sensitive to dataset-specific annotation conventions and implementation complexity.
paper_title: A Guideline-Augmented Multi-Agent Framework for Schema-as-Code Biomedical Named Entity Recognition
